question.summary: The source asked whether the reduction criterion implies the majorization inequalities between the global and local spectra of a bipartite state. Hiroshima proved the implication in 2003.
question.importance: The answer places majorization at the weak end of the established chain separable implies PPT implies undistillable implies reduction, settling where the spectral criteria of Nielsen and Kempe sit inside the hierarchy of separability and distillability criteria.

targetClauses.label: Reduction criterion implies majorization
targetClauses.text: The archived statement asks whether the reduction criterion for a bipartite state implies the majorization inequalities between the spectrum of the joint state and the spectra of its reductions.
targetClauses.resolutionCriteria: A proof of the implication, or a state satisfying the reduction criterion whose spectra violate majorization.

claims.title: Hiroshima proves the reduction criterion implies majorization
claims.text: Hiroshima shows that the reduction inequality yields an operator R of norm at most one with rho_AB^(1/2) = (rho_A^(1/2) tensor I) R, from which one constructs a substochastic matrix relating the two spectra. This gives weak submajorization, which upgrades to ordinary majorization because both spectra have unit trace, so the archived implication holds and majorization is the weakest criterion in the hierarchy.

decisions.rationale: The cited peer-reviewed theorem proves exactly the implication asked for in the archived statement.
